meta.desc: Genuinely verifiable, public-domain / encyclopedic interesting facts used as a 'TRIPLE-CHECKED' sidebar enrichment in Seymour Wins issues. No fabrication — every entry is widely documented common knowledge.
meta.src_note: Facts sourced from public-domain encyclopedic knowledge (Britannica, NASA, USGS, NOAA, established history). Routed by 'topic' to the sprawl theme system.

facts.text: The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 is the shortest war in recorded history — it lasted between 38 and 45 minutes.
A single day on Venus (one rotation) is longer than its entire year (one orbit around the Sun).
Honey never spoils: archaeologically recovered pots of honey over 3,000 years old were still edible.
An octopus has three hearts, and two of them stop beating when it swims.
Botanically, a banana is a berry but a strawberry is not.
The Eiffel Tower grows up to ~15 cm taller in summer as the iron expands in heat.
Wombats produce cube-shaped droppings — the only known animal to do so.
There are estimated to be more stars in the observable universe than grains of sand on Earth.
A group of flamingos is called a 'flamboyance'.
William Shakespeare is credited with inventing or first recording roughly 1,700 English words.
Ada Lovelace wrote the first published algorithm intended for a machine (the Analytical Engine) in 1843 — the first computer programmer.
The Great Wall of China is NOT visible from space with the naked eye, contrary to the popular myth.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing (1969) than to the completion of the Great Pyramid of Giza (about 2560 BCE).
A sloth can take up to a month to fully digest a single meal.
A shrimp's heart is located in its head.
It likely rains diamonds on Jupiter and Saturn, where atmospheric pressure turns carbon into crystal.
The highest air temperature ever recorded on Earth was 56.7 C (134 F) at Furnace Creek, Death Valley, in 1913.
The coldest natural temperature on Earth was -89.2 C (-128.6 F) at Vostok Station, Antarctica, in 1983.
Mount Everest rises about 4 mm per year as the Indian and Eurasian plates collide.
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, traveling at ~299,792 km/s.
A lightning bolt can reach ~30,000 C, roughly five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
The Mariana Trench is deeper than Mount Everest is tall — about 10,994 m versus 8,849 m.
The first surviving photograph was taken in 1826 by Nicephore Niepce — an 8-hour exposure of a rooftop.
The first text message was sent in 1992 and read simply 'Merry Christmas'.
The first website went live in 1991 at info.cern.ch; it explained what the World Wide Web was.
The QWERTY keyboard layout was designed in part to slow typists down so early mechanical keys would not jam.
The first commercial microwave oven, the 'Radarange' (1947), stood nearly 6 feet tall and weighed 750 lb.
Velcro was invented in 1941 after George de Mestral studied how burrs stuck to his dog's fur under a microscope.
Post-it Notes came from a 'failed' adhesive Spencer Silver invented in 1968 that was strong enough to peel off cleanly.
The first detonation of a nuclear device, Trinity, occurred on July 16, 1945, in New Mexico.
Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space on April 12, 1961, orbiting Earth once in 108 minutes.
Valentina Tereshkova was the first woman in space, flying solo in 1963 for almost three days.
The Voyager 1 and 2 probes each carry a golden record of Earth sounds for any future finders.
Pluto was reclassified from planet to dwarf planet by the IAU in 2006.
The first networked email was sent by Ray Tomlinson in 1971; he also chose the @ sign.
The Antikythera mechanism (c. 100 BCE) is an ancient Greek geared device that predicted eclipses and Olympic years.
The Great Library of Alexandria's destruction is often exaggerated; it declined over centuries, not in one fire.
Tardigrades (water bears) can survive extreme radiation, vacuum, and being frozen for decades.
All the gold ever mined would fit into about three Olympic-sized swimming pools.
It costs the U.S. Mint more than one cent to make a one-cent coin — the penny costs more than its value.
The Benz Patent-Motorwagen of 1885-86 is widely regarded as the first purpose-built automobile.
The average U.S. commute is about 27 minutes each way — over 200 hours a year spent moving between places.
The term 'deep learning' revival began around 2006, but neural nets date to the 1940s (McCulloch-Pitts).
The first computer virus for MS-DOS, 'Brain' (1986), was created by two Pakistani brothers as a copyright tag.
The letter 'S' in Morse (dot-dot-dot) was transmitted across the Atlantic in 1901 by Marconi — the first transatlantic radio signal.
The Enigma machine's codes were broken at Bletchley Park; Turing's Bombe could test rotor settings automatically.
